units.account: Col. Aubry has no order and holds his line south of the river, facing the bridge. Nothing is in sight.
Col. Delacroix has no order and keeps his line beside the 1st Battalion. Nothing is in sight.

Maj. Verneuil is already on the south bank opposite the northern wood when his order comes, and stays there watching its southern edge across the river. He sees nothing move in the open, and cannot see into the trees from 800 m. There is no news to send back.

Col. Brandt is told to stand where he is and show himself on the road to hold the enemy's eye. He steps his line a few paces east so that it sits across the high road in plain view, and stands there, though he would rather be advancing.

Col. Hartmann gets his order at about the second minute and marches his column across the open ground to the north-east corner of the northern wood. He then goes through the trees by the shortest line towards the southern edge, slowly because of the undergrowth, and halts just inside the trees at their southern edge at about the fifteenth minute, unseen from the river, as he was ordered. He stays in column under cover.
Maj. von Reiter has no order and holds his position, watching the open ground to the south.

summary: Red-2 marched through the northern wood as ordered, entering at its north-east corner and halting just inside its southern edge at about (950,825), unseen. The slow going in the wood used up most of the turn. Red-1 stood on the high road in view of the enemy to hold their attention, but at 1400 m from the Blue infantry no one could see it. Blue-3 watched the wood from the south bank, but at about 840 m from the Red column, and with the column hidden by the trees, it saw nothing. No other units moved and no one saw anyone; no fire or melee. The result matches the projection.
